history.summary: Sri Sri Jogomaya Kalibari on Temple Street, Nutan Para is one of the oldest and largest Kali temples in Jalpaiguri town, in the heart of the busy marketplace. The compound also houses a Shiva lingam and a shrine to Baba Lokenath, so it is known locally as the Maa Jogomaya and Baba Lokenath temple. Poet Mohit Ghosh wrote a poem about this iconic temple. Durga Puja and Jagadhatri Puja are organised with grandeur; a hawan is held every new moon and bhog must be booked by 11 AM. IDENTITY: CONFIRMED — this Jalpaiguri-town complex (not the Dagapur/Siliguri Lokenath Baba Mandir, seq 1170) matches the CSV row. Note: all early-history detail comes from visitor reviews; founding year '1920s' is weakly sourced — flag as approximate.

name: Maa Jogomaya and Baba Lokenath Temple
town_description: Jalpaiguri is a district headquarters town in north West Bengal on the banks of the Teesta river, gateway to the Dooars region. The temple sits at Nutan Para/Temple Street in the busy market area of the town.

travel.railway: Jalpaiguri Road and Jalpaiguri stations are both a few km away; New Jalpaiguri Junction (~40 km) is the major hub
travel.road: On Temple Street, Nutan Para, ward no. 7 — any local toto/auto reaches it; note reviewers report parking problems on the busy street

visitor_information.best_time: October–March; Durga Puja season is the biggest but most crowded
